key_insight: Surrogate-guided reinforcement learning enriches perovskite solar-cell recipe shortlists with candidates near high-performing measured devices, rather than demonstrating new experimental performance.
engineering_relevance: The framework could help prioritize recipes for fabrication across large composition, device-layer, and processing search spaces.
method: Generate candidate recipes using reinforcement-learning policies guided by a frozen TabPFN surrogate.
Assess neighborhood support against a reference pool of 890 measured devices.
Compare three learned policies with six baselines using 3,000 surrogate evaluations per run.
evidence_signal: Five-fold evaluation on 1,846 devices raised mean PCE from 19.68% to 23.74% through top-ten selection; top-100 neighborhood-supported hit rates reached 23–24% for PPO/RPPO versus 2.9% for random screening and 10% for the strongest baselines.
watch_item: Support weakens at stricter similarity thresholds, and the results do not establish experimental performance, seed robustness, or matched-budget advantage.
paper_title: Enrichment-Oriented Virtual Screening of Perovskite Solar Cells through Reinforcement Learning
